text:
Priya: Recap from MapleHealth renewal call — procurement/legal are blocking signature until they get a formal per-route chargeback export + an errors/audit timeline for SOC. They asked for something reproducible they can attach to their vendor risk review.
Marco: Oof. What fields did they request exactly?
Priya: They want CSV with: account_id, route, date, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd, error_code (nullable), transcript_char_count, and a redacted user identifier (ok as hashed id). 180-day window. Delivered via presigned S3 link to their procurement mailbox.
Devika: We can produce that from events_warehouse. Two cautions: (1) redact PII and hash user ids (we should use a one-way SHA256 with salt), (2) rate limit the export to avoid scan storms. We should also avoid exporting raw transcripts — include only transcript_char_count.
Rohit: For enablement I'll create a 2-page playbook showing how to ingest CSV into their chargeback system and a 15-minute walkthrough recording they can reuse. Also a quick template email they can forward to finance with the presigned link.
Marco: Product note: this is the nth customer asking for downloadable per-route exports. Let's add a backlog item: "Account export: per-route chargeback CSV + admin Console export" with acceptance criteria: documented CSV schema, configurable window (30/90/180), RBAC (account admins only), presigned S3 TTL, audit log entry for exports.
Priya: MapleHealth said renewal committee in 12 business days. They explicitly said legal won't move without the CSV — high risk.
Devika: Short-term plan: I'll run a redacted export and drop it to an ops S3 bucket with a presigned link TTL 7 days. I'll run the export during a low-traffic window and post the SHA256 salt used for hashing into the secure vault for audit.
Marco: For the long-term, scope the Console export API and UI so CS can generate exports without involving infra. Also need a security review for the hashing approach and audit trail.
Devika: Export snippet (redacts and hashes emails):
```bash
# redacted + hashed export (180d)
PS1_SALT=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id export-hash-salt --query SecretString --output text)
psql events -c "COPY (SELECT account_id, route, recorded_at::date AS date, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, (prompt_tokens+completion_tokens)*rate AS cost_usd, COALESCE(error_code,'') AS error_code, char_length(transcript) AS transcript_char_count, encode(digest(user_email || '$PS1_SALT','sha256'),'hex') AS user_hash FROM events_raw WHERE recorded_at >= now() - interval '180 days') TO STDOUT WITH CSV HEADER" > maple_export_180d.csv
# upload and presign
aws s3 cp maple_export_180d.csv s3://redwood-exports/maplehealth/ && aws s3 presign s3://redwood-exports/maplehealth/maple_export_180d.csv --expires-in 604800
```
Rohit: I'll bundle the walkthrough + sample pivot templates and attach to the onboarding repo so other CS reps can reuse.
Priya: Action items: 1) Devika to run redacted export and share presigned link by Fri EOD. 2) Rohit to prepare playbook + 15m walkthrough and sample email. 3) Marco to file product ticket for Console export MVP and tag security for RBAC/audit. 4) Priya to update MapleHealth and confirm acceptance of presigned delivery.
CS-Bot: Reminder — MapleHealth renewal review scheduled in 12 business days (calendar invite sent).
Marco: I'll add acceptance criteria to the product ticket: sample CSV attached, presign flow documented, RBAC enforced, export audit logged, and a fallback process (CS can request ops to run export).
Priya: Customer quote to capture: "We need transparent chargebacks — without a reproducible export we can't finalize allocation approvals." They emphasized speed and auditability over feature add-ons.
Devika: Pinging infra for low-impact window and will paste the presigned link here when ready.
Rohit: :thumbsup:
